correctness.rationale: From invertibility the square vectors e_i^2 form a basis, so off-diagonal Leibniz coefficients vanish. Diagonal derivations obey lambda_j=2 lambda_i on every nonzero matrix entry. In odd characteristic every weakly connected support component has solution dimension 0 or 1, the latter exactly for a Z/r cyclic edge grading, r=ord_p(2); each such component has r colorings. For invertible compatible-coloring matrices all r color blocks are square of equal size m, giving g_m(q)^r. Labelled connected-component exponential formula gives G_q(x)F_{q,r}(x^r)^((u-1)/r); p=2 all derivations vanish. Good components have at least r vertices. Weighted r-cycles and diagonal leftovers realize all d<=floor(n/r); first-stratum counts use cycles and GL_{n-r}. Exact independent rational formal-series coefficients for p=q=3,5,7 reproduce 3-adic n=4 vector [24253200,7872,48]. Finite arithmetic does not prove all dimensions or prime powers; the given combinatorial proof does.
residual_risks: Counts ordered marked matrices, not algebra isomorphism classes; finite field F_{p^e} allowed by analytic combinatorial proof, but numerical checks only small prime fields.
